ingredients.raw: 1 onion, about ¼ pound peeled and stuck with 2 whole cloves
ingredients.preparation: about ¼ pound peeled and stuck with 2 whole cloves

steps.text: Put tongue, lentils, water, bay leaf, onion with cloves, thyme, salt and pepper in a kettle and bring to boil. Let cook, uncovered, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim off and discard stem end of leek. Carefully rinse between leaves of leek and drain well. Chop green and white parts of leek; there should be about 1 ¼ cups.
Heat butter in a skillet and add chopped leek, chopped onions, garlic, salt and pepper. Cook, stirring, until onions are wilted. Add tomatoes and cook, stirring often, about 2 minutes.
When tongue and lentils have cooked 15 minutes, add leek and onion in tomato sauce. Stir and continue cooking.
Continue cooking 30 minutes longer for a total cooking time of 45 minutes. Discard onion studded with cloves and bay leaf. Add parsley and stir. Serve tongue sliced with lentils on the side.

name: Tomato-Avocado Salad With Creamy Feta Dressing
author: Ashley Lonsdale
description: With the help of a small blender or food processor, this recipe yields a rich walnut-feta dressing, ideal for drizzling over a mix of seasoned tomatoes, chickpeas and avocados. The dressing can be made without electricity by mashing the feta and mincing the walnuts, cilantro and garlic, but  if you have an appliance on hand, don’t miss out on the luscious quality of the blade-blended dressing. A word of warning: the success of this salad lives and dies by the freshness of the walnuts. Rancid walnuts will generate a rancid dressing. Before blending, smell your walnuts to make sure there are no off notes — you want the aromas to be neutral or nutty. If time and patience allow, quickly toast the nuts as outlined in the tip below.

ingredients.raw: 2 pounds ripe tomatoes (see Tips), cut into ½- to 1-inch pieces or wedges
ingredients.preparation: cut into ½- to 1-inch pieces or wedges

ingredients.raw: 1 small sweet or white onion, halved and thinly sliced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: ½ cup chopped, toasted walnuts, divided (see Tips)
½ cup chopped fresh cilantro, divided
3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice (from about 1 juicy lemon)
ingredients.item: fresh lemon juice (from about 1 juicy lemon)

ingredients.raw: 3 ounces feta, crumbled (plus feta brine if available)
1 tablespoon water, plus more as needed
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling

steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the tomatoes, chickpeas and onions with a generous pinch of salt and a dusting of pepper. Set aside for 5 to 10 minutes to marinate.

Meanwhile, make the dressing: To a small food processor or blender, add ¼ cup chopped walnuts and ¼ cup chopped cilantro, reserving the remaining for garnish. Add the lemon juice, feta, garlic and 1 tablespoon cold water (or feta brine, if the feta was packaged in brine). Blend the dressing until it begins to turn light green, adding a teaspoon or two of water as needed to loosen. Add the olive oil and pulse until just emulsified and creamy, but be careful not to over-blend or the olive oil will take on bitter notes. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

Halve the avocados and discard the pits. Slice the flesh of each side without cutting through the skin, then use a spoon large enough to scoop out the slices in one go and shingle them on a platter or in a low, wide serving bowl. Season with salt and a drizzle of olive oil.
To serve, spoon the tomato mixture onto the platter next to the sliced avocado. Drizzle the dressing over top and sprinkle with reserved walnuts and cilantro.

name: Tomato Lentil Rice With Feta Yogurt
author: Ifrah F. Ahmed
description: This deeply comforting one pot tomato-lentil rice works equally well as a side dish or as the main part of a meal. Aromatic cumin and coriander pair well with the acidity of the marinara, while the earthy turmeric gives the dish a golden brown hue. Top with a generous dollop of herby dill and feta-flecked yogurt and serve with a fresh cucumber salad. For a more protein heavy meal, serve with chicken, fish, or beef. This rice freezes very well and is the kind of dish that is great to warm up on a weekday for a delicious and quick dinner.

ingredients.raw: ½ cup jarred marinara sauce (such as Rao’s)
½ cup roughly chopped fresh cilantro

steps.text: In a medium pot over medium high heat, heat oil until it is loose and shimmering, about 1 minute. Lower the heat to medium and add onions, cover with a lid and cook, stirring occasionally as needed, until onions have softened and have light browning on the edges, about 7 minutes.
Uncover pot, add the garlic and cook until it has softened slightly, about 1 minute. Spoon the softened garlic and onions out of the pot and transfer to a bowl; set aside.

Add lentils to the same pot along with enough water to cover. Adjust the heat to medium-high, bring to a boil and cook until the lentils have softened slightly, about 14 minutes. Drain lentils in a colander and rinse briefly until the water runs clear.

Return the lentils to the pot along with the reserved onion-garlic mixture. Stir in the rice, marinara sauce, cilantro, cumin, coriander and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute until the rice starts to dry slightly.

Add the water to the pot along with the salt, adjust the heat to high and bring to a strong boil. Stir the rice mixture once more, cover the pot, and turn the heat to low. Cook undisturbed for 12 to 15 minutes, then remove from heat and let the pot rest, covered, for 5 minutes more, until the rice is tender.

While the rice cooks, combine yogurt, garlic, dill, salt, lemon juice, feta, and pepper in a bowl until all the ingredients are integrated. Place the yogurt mix in the fridge to chill while the rice finishes.
When the lentil rice is ready, uncover the pot and fluff with a fork, and serve with feta yogurt.

name: Tofu Musubi
author: Kristina Felix
description: Musubis are a traditional Hawaiian snack built to travel. Steamed rice is pressed into a nori-lined mold and wrapped to bundle the rice. Traditionally filled with grilled and glazed slices of Spam, here, the rice is topped with teriyaki glazed tofu for a vegetarian twist on the classic. And you don’t need a special musubi mold because you can rig one out of the tofu carton. Serve with sliced pineapple for dipping into the extra teriyaki pan sauce, or tuck a slice between the rice and the tofu for extra crunch and sweetness if you’d like. Assembled and cooled musubis can be wrapped in plastic wrap and refrigerated for up to two days. Eat them at room temperature straight from your jacket pocket or lunchbox.

ingredients.raw: 1 (14-ounce) package extra firm tofu, in a plastic carton
½ fresh pineapple, peeled, cored and sliced (optional)

steps.text: Open and drain the package of tofu and set aside the plastic carton. Place tofu on an upturned plate and put it in the sink. Top with another plate and place a heavy can or book on top to press the liquid out of the tofu.

Meanwhile, add rice to a medium pot with a lid and cover with cold water. Rinse and drain the rice twice, or as needed until the water runs clear when drained. Add 1 ⅓ cup water to the rinsed rice and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Once simmering, cover, lower heat to medium-low and cook undisturbed for 10 minutes. Turn off the heat but leave the lid on for 5 more minutes before uncovering the pot, fluffing the rice and allowing it to cool a bit.
While the rice cooks, make the sauce: Combine the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, ginger and garlic powder in a bowl and stir it until the sugar is mostly dissolved.

Add the oil to a medium cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Transfer the drained tofu to a cutting board and cut it in half crosswise. Cut each half into three ½-inch rectangles, then carefully place each piece into the hot skillet. Cook the tofu until browned on one side, about 5 minutes, then flip carefully. (Try not to let them break, but it’s okay if they do.) Cook pieces for 5 more minutes, flip them again, then pour in the sauce. Simmer tofu undisturbed until the liquid thickens slightly, 6 to 8 minutes, flipping once halfway through. Turn the heat off and let the tofu cool in the skillet.

To assemble the musubi, remove the plastic seal from the tofu carton and discard. Using scissors, cut the carton in half crosswise, then cut ½-inch off of one of the cut sides so that one half is shorter than the other. Nest the shorter half into the longer half, and tape it together if you’d like, to create a musubi mold that is roughly 4-inches x 2 ½-inches. Line the musubi mold with plastic wrap.

Tear both of the nori sheets in thirds, along the grain (the faint parallel lines), to make 6 ribbons that are approximately 7 ½-inches x 3-inches. Place one ribbon into the lined musubi mold so that the ends hang over the edges a bit. Scoop ⅓ cup rice into the mold and, with damp fingers, press it into the corners. Place one piece of tofu onto the rice, then fold the nori ribbon over the tofu to create a seal. Use the overhanging plastic wrap to firmly press down on the musubi, then remove it from the mold and move to a serving plate. Continue with remaining ingredients until all 6 musubis are assembled.
Pour 2 tablespoons water into the skillet with the remaining sauce and heat over medium, stirring occasionally, until it begins to simmer. Pour sauce into a small bowl.
Serve musubi at room temperature alongside the pan sauce and sliced pineapple for dipping if you’d like.

name: Tomato-Potato Salad
author: David Tanis
description: This bright potato salad is dressed with a turmeric-tinged vinaigrette. It looks especially nice with yellow or orange cherry tomatoes, to add juicy texture and emphasize the color. Cumin, nigella seeds and scallions add depth. Boil and peel the potatoes, cut them into slices or wedges and dress them, then let them marinate at cool room temperature. Just before serving, add the cherry tomatoes along with Thai basil or mint leaves.

ingredients.raw: 3 pounds medium potatoes, such as Yukon Gold
½ cup slivered scallions, white and green parts
1 pint cherry tomatoes, halved and lightly salted
Thai basil leaves or fresh mint leaves, for garnish
ingredients.item: thai basil leaves or fresh mint leaves

steps.text: Add potatoes to a large pot and boil over high heat until just done and a skewer goes in easily. Drain and let cool slightly until warm enough to handle. Peel and cut into ¾-inch slices and place in a large bowl. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, in a small jar with a lid, put vinegar, sugar, turmeric, nigella, cumin and vegetable oil. Shake jar vigorously to emulsify the dressing. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Drizzle dressing over potatoes, add scallions and gently toss everything to coat. Transfer to a serving dish.
Scatter cherry tomatoes over the top, along with basil leaves or mint leaves. The salad is best served at room temperature.
